sections.h2: Where do Taylor County property tax matters get handled?
sections.html:
Taylor County stacks its tax offices on one street in Campbellsville. The sheriff, the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) and the county clerk all work out of 203 North Court Street, so a single stop can cover a payoff, an exemption form and a lien check.

Taylor County tax offices in Campbellsville (sources: sheriff's page, PVA site, county clerk site)

The sheriff's page also links an online portal for searching and paying 2026 bills. Pop-ups must be switched on in your browser or the portal will not open.

sections.h2: What is Taylor County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Taylor County became Kentucky's 100th county out of 120 when it was organized in 1848. Settlers arrived from Virginia, Pennsylvania, Maryland and North Carolina after the Revolution, and the name honors Zachary Taylor. Its 277 square miles, 266 of them land, take the outline of a heart, and local boosters say the geographic center of Kentucky sits inside. Neighboring counties dispute that. The Civil War skirmish known as the Battle of Tebbs Bend was fought here.

Campbellsville is the seat and the only city, with Acton, Hobson, Mannsville, Saloma and Spurlington among the unincorporated communities. Marion, Casey, Adair, Green and LaRue counties surround it. The Green and Adair lines also mark the Central time boundary, and Black Gnat straddles it. Campbellsville Independent and Taylor County Schools split the school districts. In the 2020 count, 49.1 percent of residents lived in an urban area; Spencer, Todd and Trigg counties had none.

Campbellsville University anchors the economy. A study the university released in 2021 credited it with 1,866 local jobs and about $174.6 million of economic impact from its main campus. Census business data points the same way:

  • 2022 retail sales reached $1.09 billion, near $41,299 for every resident.
  • Health care and social assistance took in $245.8 million.
  • 631 employers ran payrolls in 2023, with 9,968 workers between them.

sections.h2: How do Taylor County's housing numbers read?
sections.html:
Taylor had an estimated 26,763 residents in July 2025, up 2.8 percent from 2020 and well above the 21,178 counted in 1980. Typical home value is $174,200 and typical rent is $718. Homeowners live in 68.8 percent of units, the lowest rate of the four counties, because a larger share rents: the 2020 census found 35.9 percent of occupied units were rentals, and 28.9 percent of households were one person living alone.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,217 a month for housing, against $432 for owners with none. Household income is $60,456 and the mean commute is 22.7 minutes. The Census Bureau logged just 9 building permits in 2025 against 11,247 housing units, so new construction adds little to the supply.

sections.h2: When are Taylor County tax bills due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Kentucky's collection statute makes tax payable to the sheriff by December 31 of the assessment year. Under it:

  • A bill settled by November 1 earns a 2 percent break.
  • Between that date and December 31, the printed amount applies.
  • January brings a 5 percent surcharge.
  • After January 31, 10 percent applies, with the sheriff's add-on fee from the Revenue Department's delinquency worksheet.

The clerk's website states that Taylor County bills turn delinquent on April 15 each year, when the sheriff's file closes and unpaid bills pass to the clerk.

sections.h2: What does the Taylor County clerk do with unpaid bills?
sections.html:
Collection moves to the clerk, with the county attorney writing to each owner. Two letters go out and the delinquent list runs in the Central Kentucky News Journal. A bill still open after those three notices can be offered to third-party companies, which buy it and place a lien on the property. The clerk says sales do not happen before August and that the list, with the sale date, is posted on the clerk's page as the day approaches.

The Revenue Department's worked example shows how fast a debt grows. A $1,000 bill becomes a $1,254 certificate after the penalty, the sheriff's add-on fee and an assumed commission. Then 1 percent interest accrues monthly, with a 10 percent clerk commission and, after the first notice, a 20 percent county attorney commission. Paying within five business days of the transfer avoids the attorney's share.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Taylor County assessment?
sections.html:
Meeting with the PVA at Suite 6 is the entry point. PVAs value most houses by comparing recent sales, and your conference is the time to ask which sales were used. After the meeting you file with the clerk at the end of the next workday after the May viewing period, a stretch of two weeks that includes Saturdays. A board of local owners hears the case roughly a month afterward.

Come with facts: building characteristics, insurance values, construction costs or listings of similar property. Without them the board denies the appeal. Someone you pay to represent you must be a professional such as an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, or your own employee, and needs your written authorization.

Farmland follows a separate rule. Kentucky values it at what the land earns in agriculture rather than what it would sell for, which can cut a bill sharply near cities and matters less in rural areas where the two values sit close together. Taxable personal property is listed with the PVA by May 15.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Taylor County?
sections.html: Homeowners past 65, and owners on a total-disability classification from a federal agency or a retirement system, receive $49,100 off the assessment for 2025 and 2026. File Form 62A350 at the PVA before December 31. A household gets one exemption even if both spouses qualify, and a purchaser must apply again after a sale.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when selling a Taylor County house?
sections.html: Get the sheriff's exact payoff, then ask the clerk whether the parcel carries a certificate from an earlier year. Each year's tax is the January 1 owner's own debt, and a delinquent lien can follow the land for eleven years. When an outside company holds the bill, the money goes to that company instead of the clerk.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Taylor County property tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 203 North Court Street, Suite 7, or through the online portal for 2026 payments. Call (270) 465-4351 to confirm the amount.

faqs.q: When does a Taylor County bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 15 of the following year, according to the clerk's website. The sheriff's file closes and the clerk takes over collection.

faqs.q: Will Taylor County sell my overdue tax bill to a company?
faqs.a: It can, after the three notices. The clerk says no sales happen before August, and the buyer's lien then attaches to your property.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Taylor County?
faqs.a: Take Form 62A350 to the PVA at (270) 465-5811 before December 31. The home must be your residence on January 1, and you must qualify by age or disability.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Taylor County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes, since the balance is paid out of the proceeds. Bring written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk so the closing agent can clear every open year.
